task: Write `fn minOfThree(a: Int, b: Int, c: Int) -> Int` returning the smallest of three integers.
Write `fn isPositive(n: Int) -> Bool` that is true when n is greater than zero.
Write `fn sign(n: Int) -> Int` returning -1, 0 or 1 according to the sign of n.
Write `fn cube(n: Int) -> Int` returning n multiplied by itself three times.
Write `fn rectArea(w: Int, h: Int) -> Int` returning width times height, for non-negative sides.
Write `fn lastDigit(n: Int) -> Int` returning the last decimal digit of a non-negative n.
Write `fn countNegative(xs: List[Int]) -> Int` counting the elements below zero.
Write `fn product(xs: List[Int]) -> Int` multiplying all elements; the empty list gives 1. Use fold.
Write `fn smallest(xs: List[Int]) -> Int` for a non-empty list, returning the smallest element.
Write `fn firstThree(xs: List[Int]) -> List[Int]` returning at most the first three elements.
Write `fn dropFirst(xs: List[Int]) -> List[Int]` returning the list without its first element, or empty.
Write `fn incrementAll(xs: List[Int]) -> List[Int]` adding one to every element.
Write `fn keepPositive(xs: List[Int]) -> List[Int]` keeping only elements greater than zero.
Write `fn allPositive(xs: List[Int]) -> Bool` true when every element is greater than zero.
Write `fn hasZero(xs: List[Int]) -> Bool` true when some element equals zero.
Write `fn isSorted(xs: List[Int]) -> Bool` true when the list is in non-decreasing order. Use zip and all.
Write `fn rangeSum(lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Int` summing the integers from lo up to but not including hi.
Write `fn squaresBelow(n: Int) -> List[Int]` listing the squares of 0 up to n-1; n is non-negative.
Write `fn shout(s: Str, n: Int) -> Str` repeating s n times, for non-negative n.
Write `fn doubleLength(s: Str) -> Int` returning twice the length of s.
Write `fn firstWord(s: Str) -> Str` returning the text before the first space (the whole text if no space).
Write `fn startsWithA(s: Str) -> Bool` true when s begins with the letter a.
Write `fn clean(s: Str) -> Str` trimming spaces and converting to lower case.
Write `fn countLetter(s: Str, c: Str) -> Int` counting how many characters of s equal c.
Write `fn joinLines(ls: List[Str]) -> Str` joining lines with a newline character.
Define `type Shape = Square(Int) | Rect(Int, Int)` and `fn perimeter(s: Shape) -> Int`.
Define `type Light = Red | Green | Yellow` and `fn canGo(l: Light) -> Bool` true only for Green.
Define `type Day = Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun` and `fn isWeekend(d: Day) -> Bool`.
Define `type Point = { x: Int, y: Int }` and `fn translate(p: Point, dx: Int, dy: Int) -> Point`.
Define `type Point = { x: Int, y: Int }` and `fn manhattan(a: Point, b: Point) -> Int` (sum of absolute differences).
Define `type Person = { name: Str, age: Int }` and `fn isAdult(p: Person) -> Bool` for age at least 18.
Define `type Person = { name: Str, age: Int }` and `fn rename(p: Person, name: Str) -> Person`.
Write `fn safeFirst(xs: List[Int]) -> Option[Int]` returning the first element if any.
Write `fn doubleOpt(o: Option[Int]) -> Option[Int]` doubling the value inside, keeping None.
Write `fn orZero(o: Option[Int]) -> Int` returning the value or 0.
Write `fn parseOr(s: Str, d: Int) -> Int` converting text to an integer, or d when it is not a number.
Write `fn divide(a: Int, b: Int) -> Result[Int, Str]` returning Err("zero") when b is 0.
Write `fn valueOr(r: Result[Int, Str], d: Int) -> Int` returning the Ok value or d.
Write `fn percent(part: Int, whole: Int) -> Int` returning part*100/whole for a positive whole.
Write `fn evensBelow(n: Int) -> List[Int]` listing the even numbers from 0 below n; n is non-negative.
Write `fn doubleThenAdd(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int` returning 2*a + b.
Write `fn atLeastZero(n: Int) -> Int` returning n, but 0 when n is negative.
Write `fn bigger(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int` returning the larger one.
Write `fn countDown(n: Int) -> List[Int]` listing n, n-1, ..., 1 for n >= 0 using recursion.
Write `fn digitSum(n: Int) -> Int` summing the decimal digits of a non-negative n using recursion.
Write `fn length(xs: List[Int]) -> Int` counting elements with pattern matching and recursion.
Write `fn has(xs: List[Int], x: Int) -> Bool` using pattern matching and recursion.
Write `fn sumPairs(ps: List[(Int, Int)]) -> List[Int]` adding the two numbers of each pair.
Write `fn swap(p: (Int, Str)) -> (Str, Int)` swapping the two parts.
Write `fn mean(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int` returning (a + b) / 2.
Write `fn toFahrenheit(c: Float) -> Float` converting with c * 1.8 + 32.0.
Write `fn roundedHalf(x: Float) -> Int` returning x / 2.0 rounded to an integer.
Write `fn bmiClass(bmi: Int) -> Str` returning "low" below 18, "normal" below 25, otherwise "high".
Write `fn grade(score: Int) -> Str` returning "A" from 90, "B" from 80, "C" from 70, otherwise "F".
Write `fn isLeap(y: Int) -> Bool` using the Gregorian rule.
Write `fn fizz(n: Int) -> Str` returning "Fizz" for multiples of 3, otherwise the number as text.
Write `fn nth(xs: List[Int], i: Int, d: Int) -> Int` returning the element at i or d when i is out of range.
Write `fn middle(xs: List[Int]) -> Int` returning the element at the middle index of a non-empty list.
Write `fn pairUp(xs: List[Int]) -> List[(Int, Int)]` pairing each element with its index using enumerate (index first).
Define `type Pos = Int where it > 0` and `fn halfOf(n: Pos) -> Int` returning n / 2.
Define `type Percent = Int where it >= 0 && it <= 100` and `fn invert(p: Percent) -> Percent` returning 100 minus p.
